instagram_caption:
A rip-off of Akira Kurosawa's film paid him handsomely. 🎬

In 1961 he made Yojimbo: a nameless samurai plays two rival gangs against each other. In 1964 Sergio Leone made A Fistful of Dollars, the same story set among cowboys. Nobody had bought the rights, and Toho, Kurosawa's studio, sued.

Kurosawa reportedly wrote to Leone that it was a very good movie, but it was his movie. The case settled out of court before the film reached American cinemas in 1967. Reports say Kurosawa got a share of worldwide takings, and the story goes it paid him more than Yojimbo did.

The twist: Yojimbo had borrowed too. Kurosawa reportedly named Dashiell Hammett's The Glass Key as a source, and critics hear Hammett's novel Red Harvest (1929) in it. A copy of a copy of a copy.

Which is the better version: samurai or cowboy? 👇
